summary: The rewrite closes round 1's blocking finding and three of its four minors, and I verified the replacements rather than taking them: the single-pass stripper survives the URL-in-a-string and char-literal-holding-a-quote inputs; the deny-list coverage assertion now KILLS the T1 mutation (reducing BANNED to three entries fails 2 of 15 cases, run); dropping the char branch and dropping the text-block branch each red exactly one case, so the new cases are falsifiable; the 11-vs-2 seam-implementor measurement is TRUE as measured (11 files match, 2 in binstore-backends); the git-ls-files oracle replaces the walk; and the 'exactly ONE match, LocalFsBinStore' claim is true. Two things still let a real violation through. (1) The text-block branch scans for the closing delimiter with a bare find(), so one escaped `\"""` -- the ordinary Java idiom for embedding three quotes -- blanks the ENTIRE remainder of the file: a compiling business-logic file containing Files.readString(Path.of("/etc/hostname")) below such a text block is reported `ok 1 business-logic file(s) take a seam`, which is the same class of bug the diff asserts in three places it 'cannot have at all'. (2) Four compiling business-logic files that open a real socket, a real file and the real system clock pass green, all inside families the list explicitly enumerates. Both fixes are small and local to io_seam_scan.py; this is not a commit that needs splitting.

findings.title: One escaped quote-triple in a text block blanks the rest of the file, and a real Files.readString(Path.of("/etc/hostname")) below it is reported ok -- the exact class of bug the diff says the rewrite cannot have
findings.location: scripts/io_seam_scan.py, code_only(), the `elif src.startswith('\"\"\"', i): j = src.find('\"\"\"', i + 3)` branch
findings.blocking_reason: A compiling business-logic file that reads /etc/hostname is reported clean by a gate whose entire purpose is to refuse it, and the failure blanks everything after the construct rather than just the construct.

findings.title: Four compiling business-logic files opening a real socket, a real file and the real system clock pass green -- the gaps are inside families the deny-list itself enumerates, and the success line asserts a property the deny-list cannot establish
findings.location: scripts/io_seam_scan.py BANNED (Clock.system / SocketChannel.open( / ServerSocketChannel.open( / DatagramChannel.open( / FileChannel.open( entries); scripts/check-io-seam.sh, the `ok "$COUNT business-logic file(s) take a seam for every clock, socket and store"` line
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED in a throwaway worktree at the staged bytes. Four files written under ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/, all compiled clean by javac, all staged, `./scripts/check-io-seam.sh` printed `ok 4 business-logic file(s) take a seam for every clock, socket and store`, exit 0. Per-file scanner runs each reported 0 violations.

  1. EvadeTickClock -- `Clock.tickSeconds(ZoneOffset.UTC).instant()`. The list carries `Clock.system` deliberately as a PREFIX, the comment explaining that it must cover systemUTC/systemDefaultZone/system. java.time.Clock has four families of static factory; tickSeconds, tickMinutes and tickMillis all document 'using best available system clock' and all return a real clock. The prefix stops one family short.
  2. EvadeAsyncFile -- `AsynchronousFileChannel.open(FileSystems.getDefault().getPath("/etc/hostname"))`. `FileChannel.open(` IS listed; the `\b` anchor on the owner means `AsynchronousFileChannel.open` does not match it (preceded by `s`). `FileSystems.getDefault().getPath` is the third unlisted way to make a Path, after Path.of and Paths.get which are both listed.
  3. EvadeAsyncSocket -- `AsynchronousSocketChannel.open()`. SocketChannel.open(, ServerSocketChannel.open( and DatagramChannel.open( are all listed; the two Asynchronous* siblings in the same package are not, and the same `\b` anchor means the listed entries cannot reach them.
  4. EvadeSocketFactory -- `javax.net.SocketFactory.getDefault().createSocket(host, port)`. Opens a real TCP connection, names no banned construct.

I accept that a deny-list cannot be complete, and the scanner header says so accurately ('catches the constructs named below and nothing else'). Two things make this more than that concession. First, these are not exotic routes -- they are siblings inside families the list explicitly enumerates, each closable by one line, and the coverage assertion in everyBANNEDConstructIsREFUSED gives false confidence here: it proves every entry that EXISTS has a sample, and says nothing about the entry that should exist. Second, the gate's success line makes an AFFIRMATIVE claim it did not check -- 'N business-logic file(s) take a seam for every clock, socket and store'. That is a statement about a property; what was actually established is 'N file(s) named none of the 31 banned constructs'. Non-negotiable 4 is about not claiming more than was done, and this line is the one every future author reads. AGENTS.md's new paragraph and code-structure.md's new paragraph both illustrate incompleteness with reflection and with a dependency's API -- neither names the cheapest route, an unlisted sibling in plain source, which is what all four of these are.

Fix: add the five entries (Clock.tick, AsynchronousFileChannel.open(, AsynchronousSocketChannel.open(, AsynchronousServerSocketChannel.open(, SocketFactory.getDefault(), FileSystems.getDefault() -- with samples, which the coverage assertion will demand), and reword the ok line to state what was checked rather than what is hoped.
findings.blocking_reason: Three of the four files reach a real socket, a real file and the real system clock in plain source with no reflection, and the gate answers with a green line asserting they take a seam.

findings.title: `.openStream(` and `.openConnection(` are anchored on the member but not on the receiver, so calling that method ON A SEAM is refused as 'reaches a socket directly'
findings.location: scripts/io_seam_scan.py, _shape() when `owner` is empty (head = ''), for the entries ('.openStream(', SOCKET) and ('.openConnection(', SOCKET)

findings.title: Round 1's false superlative was replaced in three of the four places it appeared; scripts/check-io-seam.sh still carries it verbatim, and it is still false as measured
findings.failure_scenario:
Round 1 raised 'The exemption argument's superlative is false as measured, and it is restated in four places'. The replacement measurement landed in three: the backlog cell ('ELEVEN src/main files match implements ... against this module's TWO'), IoSeamGateTest's class javadoc ('review MEASURED that eleven src/main files match ... FIVE TIMES WIDER'), and code-structure.md rule 3 ('eleven src/main files implement one of the five seams against that module's two'). I verified that measurement independently and it is TRUE: `git grep -lE 'implements .*(BinStore|Sequencer|SubscriptionTransport|Membership|Clock)' -- '*/src/main/java/*.java'` returns exactly 11 files, of which exactly 2 are under binstore-backends/.

The fourth copy is unchanged. scripts/check-io-seam.sh still reads: '`LocalSequencer implements Sequencer` and holds more business logic / than any other file in the tree, so that carve-out would license I/O exactly / where the rule matters most.' (The sentence wraps across two comment lines, which is presumably why a grep for the phrase missed it.) MEASURED by line count over the 103 tracked src/main files: sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/ChainReplay.java is 604 lines, LocalSequencer.java is 578. By the only proxy available for 'holds more business logic', LocalSequencer is not the largest file in the tree -- ChainReplay is, and it implements no seam. The claim is unmeasured and wrong in the one file a reader opens first when the gate fires, since the gate's own failure text points at this script.

Minor and not worth its own round if the two majors are being fixed anyway -- but it is an open finding the diff was expected to close, so recording it rather than letting it drop.
